scope: Team startup admission, request-budget metadata, and workspace binding
findings: TeamRun read errors could be collapsed into absent data and remove the configured team-wide max_model_calls ceiling.
Missing, unreadable, and malformed workspace sidecars shared the same Option result and could be interpreted as an intentional unbound workspace.
A failed worker registry build could exit the loop without cancelling the still-running TeamRun.
changes: Added checked workspace binding loading with missing-vs-invalid semantics, identity checks, canonical root and write-scope revalidation, and run_dir/team_id-scoped cache keys.
Made TeamRun retrieval required for registry construction so global request budgets cannot disappear on read failure.
Invalid binding or registry startup failure now emits a specific audit event, requests cancellation, and closes pending rework.
Validated bindings are cached by canonical run_dir plus team_id; trusted hits avoid repeated filesystem canonicalization per phase.
regression_tests_added: missing binding remains an explicit unbound result
corrupt and wrong-team-id sidecars are rejected
tampered canonical write paths are rejected
same team ID in different run directories does not share cached binding

static_checks.rustfmt: passed for project_workspace_api.rs, workswarm_api/registry_builder.rs, and workswarm_api/runtime.rs
static_checks.git_diff_check: passed for the three changed Rust files

rust_test.required: at least 6 GB available and less than 80% used

limitations: Rust compilation, unit-test execution, full cancellation persistence, and runtime recovery behavior remain unverified.
